t333: What is GEO, and how does it differ from SEO
t334: SEO optimises for a list of traditional links. GEO optimises for
t336: : an engine must retrieve the page, parse it, resolve the entity and find a passage worth citing. They overlap (crawler access, structure, metadata), but a page can rank well and remain hard to cite — which is why citability is scored separately.
t337: How long before AI engines cite me
t338: Nobody can promise a date, and any tool that does is guessing. What can be measured: whether crawlers are allowed, whether the entity resolves, whether a passage is citable and how quickly a change is announced (IndexNow). The report provides these, plus the projected score once fixes are delivered.
t339: Does the Ops loop query ChatGPT or Gemini without me
t340: No, by design. Live collections use
t342: , configured per client, stored on the server and never returned to the browser. Each run is bounded (5 prompts per batch, 2 batches), creates a dataset to review, and the scheduler is disabled by default. Detected mentions remain provisional until you confirm or reject them.
t343: Can the article pipeline publish by itself
t344: No. Seven quality gates block publication while they fail (title, metadata, answer-first, FAQ, length, lists, entities), and even after they pass, sending requires explicit approval. Content is sent to WordPress
